audit_findings.title: The Sisecam stake is residual to substantial current debt and may require further capital
audit_findings.magnitude: $277.5 million bridge addition, equal to $20.67 per diluted unit; $39.2 million 2026 contribution; $104.5 million Sisecam current debt at 2025-12-31
audit_findings.mechanism: The equity-method carrying amount is added through the valuation bridge even though realizable equity value depends on investee debt, losses, refinancing, future capital requirements and distributions.
audit_findings.evidence: As discussed in Note 1 to the financial statements, the Company has $104.5 million of debt classified as current liabilities as of December 31, 2025, with certain borrowings maturing in October 2026 and December 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The June 2026 bridge amount is effectively Sisecam's $277.475 million equity-method carrying value after the $39.2 million contribution, not a demonstrated fair value. Sisecam then produced a $21.465 million first-half loss and no distributions. A material write-down could change the conclusion: removing the full bridge addition would reduce base value from $153.11 to about $132.44 per unit and the 30% buy-below level from $107.18 to about $92.71. The record demonstrates the exposure and recent cash consumption, but not the stake's realizable value or the size of any required discount.
audit_findings.action: Obtain Sisecam's June 2026 debt maturity and liquidity schedule, refinancing terms, approved capital plan, distribution forecast and an independent equity valuation; rerun the bridge using supported fair-value downside cases without treating contributed capital as automatic value creation.

audit_findings.title: A positive perpetual growth rate may capitalize a wasting mineral base without replacement economics
audit_findings.magnitude: Terminal value represents 45.6% to 50.9% of scenario value; required adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Positive 2.5% perpetual growth raises terminal owner earnings even though reserve depletion or replacement spending may not be charged in owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Metallurgical coal is a finite and declining resource, particularly in industrialized nations.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a material model-design issue because roughly half of each scenario depends on the terminal value. Coal is explicitly finite, NRP no longer reports reserve estimates for its royalty properties, and cash capital expenditure is near zero because lessees perform the mining. Accounting depletion therefore does not establish that owner earnings bears the economic cost of replacing exhausted royalty interests. The record demonstrates finite-resource exposure but cannot quantify remaining coal-property life or replacement economics.
audit_findings.action: Prepare property-level reserve or economic-tonnage runoff schedules, reconcile accounting depletion to economic depletion, and rerun all scenarios using finite-life cash flows, zero or negative terminal growth, and separately supported replacement-acquisition spending.

audit_findings.title: The numerator may include the general partner's 2% claim while the denominator contains only common units
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum identified mismatch is 2%: $2.63 million of the $131.5 million anchor and approximately $3.06 per unit of base value
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash flows and bridge assets attributable to the GP would be assigned to common units if the 2% GP interest was not removed from the numerator and bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The general partner is entitled to receive 2 % of such distributions.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes a separate 2% GP participation, but the supplied record does not establish whether the valuation already removed it. Even assuming the entire valuation should be reduced by 2%, base value would fall from $153.11 to about $150.05 per unit and the buy-below level from $107.18 to about $105.04. The $113.72 market price would remain above the buy-below threshold by about $8.68, so this issue alone is not reasonably capable of changing the stated purchase conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace each historical owner-earnings figure and bridge component to common-unitholder allocation; if the GP claim was retained, rerun numerator and bridge at the common holders' 98% share.

audit_findings.title: Unrecorded environmental obligations could become claims ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Expected cleanup, reclamation or continuing water-treatment liabilities would reduce owner earnings or require a liability deduction in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We could become liable under federal and state Superfund and waste management statutes if our lessees are unable to pay environmental cleanup costs relating to hazardous substances.
audit_findings.explanation: No demonstrated valuation error or presently quantified obligation is supplied. NRP reported no material environmental charges, no known material contamination and reliance on lessee liability, reclamation bonds and indemnities. Those protections do not eliminate landowner exposure if a lessee or indemnitor fails, particularly for continuing discharges from reclaimed sites. Without site-specific costs, bond coverage and counterparty credit data, the record cannot establish either immateriality or a material expected-value deduction.
audit_findings.action: Obtain a site-by-site schedule of closed and active properties, estimated reclamation and perpetual-treatment costs, bond coverage, indemnities, permit holders, lessee and surety credit quality, known notices or contamination, and legal probability assessments; deduct probability-weighted exposure or rerun downside cases if supported.
